label: Extrovert
description: Automate LinkedIn campaigns, prospects, comments and direct messages

operations.name: list_team_members
operations.description: Returns all users visible to the current user inside their selected team. Optionally narrow the result by `registrationType` — e.g. to show only invited members or only managed accounts.

operations.name: list_campaigns
operations.description: Returns all campaigns visible to the current user (both types: `TARGET_USER` and `KEYWORD` — user-facing 'Prospects campaign' and 'Topic campaign' respectively).

operations.name: get_campaign
operations.description: Loads full details of a single campaign, including the linked Voice, the whole `commenting` policy, and the full outreach settings (warm up, connection requests, direct messages).

operations.name: create_campaign
operations.description:
Creates a new campaign. The campaign owner must already have a Voice.

Two types (backend values `TARGET_USER` and `KEYWORD` correspond to user-facing 'Prospects campaign' and 'Topic campaign' respectively):
- `TARGET_USER`: engages with a specific list of LinkedIn profiles.
- `KEYWORD`: discovers posts by topic bindings.

The engagement-automation fields `skipTeammatesLeads` and `outreach` apply to `TARGET_USER` (Prospects) campaigns only. For `KEYWORD` (Topic) campaigns they do not apply — omit them (or leave them off).

operations.name: update_campaign
operations.description:
Updates the editable fields of an existing campaign. `id`, `name`, `voiceId` and `skipTeammatesLeads` are required (full replace). Backend types `TARGET_USER` and `KEYWORD` correspond to user-facing 'Prospects campaign' and 'Topic campaign' respectively.

**`KEYWORD` campaigns: only `name` and the comment policy are editable.** The backend rejects with a 409 state-conflict whenever `skipTeammatesLeads`, an explicitly passed `outreach.connectionRequests.enabled`, or an explicitly passed `outreach.directMessages.enabled` differs from the current value. Omitting the optional `outreach` and `commenting` objects means "no change" and is always safe.

operations.name: start_campaign
operations.description: Activates a campaign (sets `isActive` to `true`): the post feed resumes updating, DM drafts are suggested again, and connection requests start being sent per the campaign's settings. The campaign must be properly configured first (a Voice, and either a ProspectList for `TARGET_USER` — user-facing 'Prospects campaign' — or Monitored Topics bound to the campaign for `KEYWORD` — user-facing 'Topic campaign').

operations.name: stop_campaign
operations.description: Pauses a campaign (sets `isActive` to `false`): the post feed stops updating, no DM drafts are suggested, and no connection requests are sent until the campaign is started again. Existing posts in the approval queue are preserved.

operations.name: create_prospect_list
operations.description: Creates a new prospect list inside the given campaign and seeds it with the provided LinkedIn profile URLs. The backend validates URLs and may reject some as invalid, duplicates, or out-of-limit. The response describes which URLs were submitted, rejected, or already existed elsewhere. Profile existence is verified asynchronously after this call: a URL can be accepted into `submittedUrls` and still be dropped later — check Get Prospect List for the final prospect count before reporting how many were actually added.

operations.name: get_prospect_list
operations.description: Loads a single prospect list by id, including counters and the parent campaign id.

operations.name: add_prospects_to_list
operations.description: Adds LinkedIn profile URLs to an existing prospect list. Same validation and duplicate rules as create-list. The response describes which URLs were accepted, rejected, or skipped as duplicates.

operations.name: list_prospects
operations.description: Returns visible prospects with their campaign/list bindings and optional pagination information. Use `listId` to scope to a single list, or pass broader filter arrays for campaign-wide prospect management. This endpoint returns existing prospects only — it does not add them. To add new LinkedIn profiles, add their URLs to a prospect list (`create-list` or `add-users-to-list`).

operations.name: get_prospect
operations.description: Loads one prospect by id with the current campaign/list bindings, flags, connection data, and lightweight statistics.

operations.name: replace_prospect_notes
operations.description: Replaces the relationship note on a real LEAD prospect. Empty text clears it. Existing campaign permissions apply; drafts and automation state are unchanged. Notes add context for comment and DM generation. Generation already receives relevant post and message-history context, so repeating it in Notes is usually unnecessary. Focus on additional relationship context.

operations.name: mark_prospect_important
operations.description: Single-prospect operation: updates the important flag for one prospect.

operations.name: list_comments
operations.description: Lists one campaign's comment feed for an owner and review state. Results include the post, author, effective prospect context, current draft, state, and only actions valid now. `plannedAt` fills only when the campaign spaces approved comments with a posting interval — null means posting starts right after approval. This action does not change feed state. After a mutation — approving or skipping a comment — restart paging from `offset = 0`, because a page taken at a stale offset can skip or repeat records; this matters most in `Need approval`, which is re-ranked on every request, while the other views are ordered by lifecycle transition time and do not reorder.

operations.name: get_comment
operations.description: Returns the current owner-global comment by postId and ownerId across every state. The read is non-destructive and is the recovery check after an ambiguous write. `plannedAt` fills only when the campaign spaces approved comments with a posting interval — null means posting starts right after approval.

operations.name: set_comment_draft
operations.description: Sets the exact comment text for later review and approval. It creates an ordinary draft when none exists and never calls Extrovert generation. If the text includes the post author's full LinkedIn name or a leading part of it, Extrovert automatically tags the author once when publishing, preferring the most complete matching name. Match a literal leading part of the LinkedIn name, preserving all leading emoji and the exact spelling. A matching name must contain at least two letters; emoji-only prefixes are skipped. It does not post the comment. The comment identity is postId + ownerId and the change is owner-global: it also applies to sibling campaign activities of the same owner, even when the feed context came from one campaign.

operations.name: approve_comment
operations.description: Approves the current owner-global comment/reaction and queues the consequential LinkedIn action. Success means the command was accepted for the existing Pending/publication lifecycle, not that the comment is already live. Use Get comment when current state is needed. The comment identity is postId + ownerId and the change is owner-global: it also applies to sibling campaign activities of the same owner, even when the feed context came from one campaign.

operations.name: skip_comment
operations.description: Moves the owner-global comment out of the active review flow without posting a comment or reaction. Use unskip to restore a Skipped comment to review. The comment identity is postId + ownerId and the change is owner-global: it also applies to sibling campaign activities of the same owner, even when the feed context came from one campaign.

operations.name: list_conversations
operations.description: Lists an owner's LinkedIn conversations in the required inbox view: needs-reply, for-review (For Review), auto, unread, all, snoozed or ended. It returns preview, unread count, active workflow state, and valid next actions without marking anything read.

operations.name: get_conversation
operations.description: Returns one LinkedIn conversation, its unique active reply, and a bounded delivered-message page. Reading does not clear unread state unless markAsRead is true. Use offset 0 for the latest page and increase it to load older messages.

operations.name: prepare_reply
operations.description: Prepares one reviewable reply for a conversation from the exact supplied text, without Extrovert generation. It returns the exact dmId required for Send reply and never sends in the same call. Text that repeats a message the owner sent in this conversation in the last 24 hours (ignoring extra whitespace) is rejected with a conflict whose message starts with "Duplicate reply:", and nothing is prepared.

operations.name: edit_reply
operations.description: Sets the exact effective text of an existing reviewable reply. It does not send the message.

operations.name: send_reply
operations.description: Sends the exact prepared dmId to the LinkedIn prospect. Queued (the default) accepts the reply for the owner's normal scheduler interval and returns its process ID, not provider confirmation. Immediate waits for explicit provider acceptance, not a read receipt. An uncertain immediate outcome may already have sent the reply. History changed leaves the stale reply unsent and refreshes the conversation. A reply whose text repeats a message the owner sent in this conversation in the last 24 hours (ignoring extra whitespace) is never sent: the call fails with a conflict whose message starts with "Duplicate reply:", or a queued send ends as History changed with error code duplicate-reply.

operations.name: snooze_conversation
operations.description: Postpones a conversation until the start of an exact calendar day in the owner's timezone. Until then it is Snoozed: Extrovert recommends and sends nothing in it, and a current attention reason is cleared. Works whether or not the conversation has a recommendation. Does not send or generate a message.
